parsedVerdict.reasoning:
src/application/task-service.ts is an application-layer use-case service, and what it does fits that role. TaskService coordinates the use cases createUser, createProject, createTask, listTasks and markDone. It gets data only through repository interfaces from the domain layer, which are passed into its constructor. It builds entities, checks input and throws domain error types.

Nothing in the file belongs to infrastructure. It has no persistence code (no SQL, file I/O or storage details), no transport code (no HTTP requests, responses, status codes or routing) and no framework code. Generating IDs with randomUUID is a normal concern for an application service.

One point is borderline. The file holds some rules that could live in the domain layer: markDone throws ConflictError when a task is already done, and isTaskStatus copies the list of allowed TaskStatus values. Placing these in the application service is a mild "anemic domain" smell, where the domain types hold data but not their own rules. It does not meet the rubric's failure condition, though. That condition covers persistence, transport or framework logic in a domain file, or business rules in an infrastructure or presentation file. Checking preconditions and enforcing use-case rules inside an application service is accepted practice. No ADR text was provided that would require these rules to sit in domain entities.
